identity.description: Bright Data is a web data platform (proxy networks, Web Unlocker, Scraping Browser, SERP API, Web Scraper API/datasets) run by Bright Data Ltd. The docs, GitHub org, and MCP server all describe this product.
identity.identity_notes: Docs at docs.brightdata.com, MCP repo under github.com/brightdata owned by Bright Data Ltd (MIT footer), and the product name matches the assignment hint brightdata.com. The vendor's own pages confirm identity.

auth.oauth_flows: Remote MCP server (mcp.brightdata.com) uses OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), a resource parameter, dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), and a single scope 'mcp'. OAuth is for the MCP server only; the REST API uses API tokens.
auth.scopes_notes: Single 'mcp' scope for the MCP OAuth flow. No scope model is documented for the REST API token.

resources: Web Scraper API scrapers and snapshots
read_ops: Retrieve Web Scraper API snapshot results by snapshot ID (available 30 days after job completes)
List and inspect scrapers (MCP tools search_scrapers, get_scraper_details)
List account zone passwords (Account Management API)
write_ops: Deliver existing snapshot to cloud storage (POST /datasets/v3/deliver/{snapshot_id})
Create additional API keys (admin only, in account settings)
Manage zones (Account Management API, not fully verified)
api.limitations: Docs describe proxy access, Web Unlocker, Scraping Browser, SERP, Scrapers, Functions and Marketplace at a high level; the API reference fetch did not confirm full CRUD coverage. Rate limits not stated in fetched content. Sandbox/trial not stated. Only admins can generate API keys; each user can generate only one key.

claims.value: Two primary authentication methods: API Access (API key/token) and Native Access (proxy username and password).

claims.value: API token is sent in the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme and is required for every API request.

claims.value: A default API key is created at account creation; more keys are created in Account settings via Add API key.
claims.quote: We create a default key for you upon account creation automatically.

claims.value: Only admins can generate API keys; each user can generate only one API key.
claims.quote: only admins can generate API keys.

claims.value: API key is shown only once after generation.
claims.quote: Once generated, your API key will only be shown once.

claims.value: Every new account includes 5,000 free requests per month for the MCP server; team free tier is shared across users.
claims.quote: Every new account includes 5,000 free requests per month.

claims.value: Official MCP server repo github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp, owned by the brightdata org, MIT licensed.

open_questions: Whether a trial or sandbox exists for the REST API beyond the 5,000 free requests per month; not established.
Rate limits for the REST API and MCP server are not stated in fetched content.
Versions conflict: MCP registry entry shows 4.3.0 while npm @brightdata/mcp shows 1.7.0 in search summaries; not reconciled.
The Python SDK env var name is inconsistent across sources (BRIGHTDATA_API_TOKEN vs BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY); verify in the SDK code.
Official JavaScript SDK GitHub repo URL not confirmed.
Whether free-tier request quota (5,000/mo) is 'requests' or 'credits' is inconsistent across pages.
Full API reference breadth (CRUD coverage for zones, datasets, SERP) was not fully fetched; breadth rated Medium.
The docs.brightdata.com/general/account/api-token page returned 404 on direct fetch; admin rule relies on the authentication page.
Whether admin_approval should be the tier: new accounts get an automatic default key, so the practical gate for a solo developer may be lower than admin approval implies.
Remote MCP OAuth token refresh behavior is not documented in fetched content.
